title: Installing and Managing Plugins
one_liner: Install plugins by name from a known marketplace, choose a scope, and manage them in /plugin or from the shell.

core.title: Install is name@marketplace, with review first
core.body: `/plugin install commit-commands@claude-plugins-official` opens the plugin's details, where you review what it adds and pick a scope. The details show components and, for official plugins, a context cost estimate.
core.why: A plugin can run hooks and MCP servers. Review before installing.

quotes.text: this command doesn't install right away: it opens the `/plugin` panel on that plugin's details
quotes.label: Install plugins > Install a plugin

quotes.text: A plugin can run hooks and MCP servers, so read the pane before you install.
quotes.label: Install plugins > Install a plugin

diagram.caption: Installing a plugin in a session

core.title: Scope is a settings file
core.body: User scope writes to `~/.claude/settings.json`, project scope to the committed `.claude/settings.json`, local scope to `.claude/settings.local.json`. Local overrides project, which overrides user.
core.why: Project scope enables the plugin for collaborators but does not download it; each runs the install once per clone.

quotes.text: the local setting overrides the project setting, and the project setting overrides the user setting
quotes.label: Install plugins > Choose an install scope

quotes.text: Committing that entry turns the plugin on for your collaborators but doesn't download it to their machines.
quotes.label: Install plugins > Choose an install scope

core.title: Add a marketplace before installing from it
core.body: Only the official marketplace is added automatically. Add others with `/plugin marketplace add` and a GitHub `owner/repo`, a git URL, a local path or a hosted `marketplace.json` URL.
core.why: An install command naming an unknown marketplace fails until the marketplace is added.

quotes.text: Claude Code has to know about a marketplace before you can install from it
quotes.label: Install plugins > Add a marketplace

core.title: Updates apply to the next session
core.body: Auto-update is on for official marketplaces and off for others. The running session keeps the loaded version; run `/reload-plugins` to apply an update now.
core.why: An updated plugin does not change behaviour mid-session until you reload.

quotes.text: Plugins update automatically when the marketplace they came from has auto-update turned on.
quotes.label: Install plugins > Keep plugins updated

quotes.text: The running session keeps the versions it already loaded.
quotes.label: Install plugins > Keep plugins updated

core.title: Same operations in the shell
core.body: `claude plugin install|enable|disable|uninstall|update` change the same settings as `/plugin`. Shell installs default to user scope; pass `--scope project` or `--scope local`.
core.why: Setup scripts can install plugins without opening a session.

quotes.text: Run `claude plugin install` in your shell to install a plugin without starting a Claude Code session, for example from a setup script.
quotes.label: Install plugins > Install from your shell

practice.title: Install an official plugin

practice.variation: Install at local scope instead and check `.claude/settings.local.json`.

practice.title: Manage from the shell
steps: Start a session and confirm its commands are gone
practice.check: The plugin's commands disappear and return.

gotchas: There is no command that updates every plugin at once; update per plugin or per marketplace.
Start local marketplace paths with `./` or `../`; a bare `name/name` is read as a GitHub repository.
Include `https://` on marketplace URLs; a bare host path is rejected.
On a new machine, the official marketplace is not registered until an interactive session runs. Scripts should add it first.

cheatsheet.meaning: Panel: Discover, Installed, Marketplaces, Errors tabs.
Install from the shell at project scope.
Add a marketplace and install in one command.
Apply plugin changes in the current session.

recall.q: Which scope wins when a plugin is set in several?
Does project scope install the plugin for teammates?
recall.a: No. It enables it; each teammate installs once per clone.

recall.q: When does an auto-updated plugin take effect?
recall.a: In the next session, or after `/reload-plugins`.
